Subject: Clarify billing for long-context summarization workload

Hi Ben,

Quick one from our infra/finance review — we run a nightly summarization job that ingests full user histories (averaging ~18k tokens, peak ~28k) and then calls your API for a single summarize/generate per document. Procurement wants to understand how Redwood will bill:

- Do you charge against the model context window (e.g., 32k) or only the actual tokens sent/returned?
- How does KV/prefix reuse factor in across repeated calls for the same document?
- What rounding/minimum rules apply (per-request minimums, billing quantum, etc.)?

We're exploring a 12-month committed unit discount and want to model cost precisely — I've attached a small sample of our daily job sizes (sample-usage.csv).

Can you confirm or point me to a short worked example? If helpful we can hop on a quick call early next week.

Thanks,

Tom — thanks for the clear summary and the sample file, that's really helpful. High-level answers first, then we can follow up with a short call and a couple of worked numbers.

1) Billing basis: we bill on the actual token consumption per request (input tokens + output tokens) — not the nominal model max context. That means if you send 18k tokens + we return 1k tokens, billing is on 19k tokens for that call.

2) KV/prefix reuse: Redwood applies automatic prefix caching for repeated prompts within the same "conversation" or if you use session tokens. When prefix reuse applies, only delta tokens (new tokens not covered by the cached KV) are billed for inference compute. There are limits: cache hits are applied when the request exactly matches a cached prefix boundary and the cached item is still warm.

3) Rounding / minimums: for our hosted plans we charge in 100-token quanta with a 1000-token monthly minimum per active API key for sales-tier enterprise pilots by default — but that can be reconfigured under a committed contract. Rounding is upward to the nearest quantum per call for metering; we also provide monthly invoice-level smoothing for high-volume customers to avoid microbilling noise.

I've attached a short PDF with step-through examples (billing-examples.pdf). If you want, Karthik can add a KV-reuse example showing how repeated nightly runs would be accounted.

Subject: Internal: Worked KV + rounding examples for BrightCart

Ben / Vanessa — worked up a couple of concrete examples to paste into the customer reply (attached kv-reuse-examples.csv). Key things to call out so BrightCart can model costs precisely:

- Example A (no cache): input 18,000 tokens + output 1,000 tokens -> meter = 19,000 tokens -> rounded up to 19,100 tokens (100-token quantum) -> billed units = 19,100.

- Example B (full prefix cached across runs): if the first 12,000 tokens are cached and reused across the nightly runs, the per-call delta might be 6,000 input + 1,000 output = 7,000 tokens -> rounded to 7,000 (already quantum-aligned) -> billed units = 7,000. For monthly cost estimates multiply by run frequency and apply committed discount.

- Minimums interplay: with the default 1,000-token monthly minimum per API key we put a floor that only matters for very low-volume keys; for your scale it's negligible, but for modeling we can remove that floor under committed terms.

- Commit pricing behavior: committed discounts apply to billed tokens after rounding and after any invoice-level smoothing credits. Example: 20% commit discount on billed tokens -> you pay on 80% of the billed token quantity. We can also offer a blended effective quantum (e.g., 500-token billing quantum) as a concession for large monthly commitments if you're concerned about churn noise.

I'll attach the CSV. happy to run a short model with the sample you supplied and send a one-pager.

Karthik

Tom / Lara — quick consolidated reply and proposed next steps. Attached is a short chart and a proposed commit term sheet (proposed-commit-terms.pdf). Highlights:

- Metering: actual tokens consumed (input + output) are billed; not the model max context.
- Quantum & rounding: hosted metering uses 100-token quanta by default and rounds up per call; for committed 12-month deals we can set the quantum to 500 tokens to reduce rounding loss.
- KV / prefix reuse: when your nightly job sees repeatable prefixes (e.g., stable customer histories) Redwood will reuse KV cache and only bill the delta tokens — we included an example where reuse drops per-call billing from ~19k tokens to ~7k tokens.
- Minimums: the standard 1,000-token per-key monthly minimum is removable under a commit. We'll remove it for BR-4592.

Proposed commercial concession for modeling: 12-month commit for 10M billed tokens/month (pre-discount) -> 22% committed discount, 500-token quantum, waived per-key minimum, monthly invoice smoothing. We'll send a formal SOW if that band looks right.
